title: Check Point describes Volant Manticore, a new Iran-nexus espionage group targeting Cyprus and Saudi Arabia
date_note: Date of Check Point Research's post; it traces activity back to at least September 2025.

key_findings: Check Point Research says with high confidence that Volant Manticore is a previously undocumented Iran-nexus group, and links it to Iran's MOIS with medium confidence.
It says the group appears to be a spin-off of former MuddyWater operators (medium confidence).

Cyprus was the primary focus, with telecommunications, aviation and critical infrastructure as key sectors; in September 2026 the group shifted its focus to Saudi Arabia, with phishing aimed at healthcare.
Tools named: the KuboShell backdoor, the Homa Framework and legitimate RMM tools (NetLock RMM, N-able RMM, MeshCentral).
recommendations: Scrutinize unexpected CVs, archives and external documents, keep an inventory of approved remote administration tools, enforce strong MFA and watch for unusual authentication activity.

place: Cyprus (primary target country per Check Point)
geo_basis: country; Check Point names Cyprus as the group's primary espionage focus
summary: Check Point Research says Volant Manticore is a previously undocumented Iran-nexus espionage group, assessed with high confidence, and links it to Iran's MOIS with medium confidence. It says activity goes back to at least September 2025, with Cyprus the primary focus and, from September 2026, Saudi Arabia, including phishing aimed at healthcare. Check Point names the KuboShell backdoor and the Homa Framework among its tools.
plain: Security firm Check Point says a newly described Iran-linked group spies on organisations in Cyprus and, more recently, Saudi Arabia, using phishing lures and a backdoor called KuboShell.
exec: Check Point reports an Iran-nexus espionage group targeting telecom, aviation, critical infrastructure and, more recently, Saudi healthcare organisations.
action: Check Point advises scrutinizing unexpected CVs, archives and external documents, keeping an inventory of approved remote administration tools, and enforcing strong MFA.
impact: Check Point says Cyprus was the primary focus, with telecommunications, aviation and critical infrastructure as key sectors.

validation.note: Check Point Research's own report (vendor primary); no independent publisher read.

review.note: Compared confidence levels, MOIS/MuddyWater, targets, tools and advice against the Check Point post
